title: Fix navbar 'Get In Touch' raw text and hamburger menu dropdown background

requirements.summary: Fix the 'Get In Touch' / 'Contact Us' navigation link to render as human-readable text using the centralized translations system in both desktop and mobile views across all three language modes
acceptanceCriteria: The 'Get In Touch' / 'Contact Us' nav item renders as readable, human-readable text in the desktop navbar.
The same nav item renders correctly in the mobile hamburger menu.
The label displays correctly in all three language modes: English, Hindi, and Marathi.
No raw translation key strings, escaped characters, or template literal artifacts are visible for this nav item.

file_operations.description: Locate the 'Get In Touch' / 'Contact Us' navigation link in the NavBar component that is currently rendering as raw technical text. Identify whether the issue is an incorrect translation key lookup, missing translation entry, or improper string interpolation. Fix the rendering so it uses the correct translation key via the t() function from useLanguage() hook. Ensure both the desktop navigation links array and the mobile hamburger menu render the same corrected label. Verify the translation key exists in frontend/src/translations/translations.ts for all three languages (en, hi, mr). Test that the label displays correctly in both nav contexts and all language modes.

requirements.summary: Fix the mobile hamburger menu dropdown background to always be solid white regardless of scroll position
acceptanceCriteria: Opening the hamburger menu displays a dropdown with a solid white background.
The dropdown background remains solid white when the user scrolls the background page while the menu is open.
The dropdown does not appear transparent, semi-transparent, or change appearance based on the navbar's scroll state (transparent vs. solid).
All nav links within the dropdown remain readable against the solid white background.
Behavior is consistent across mobile viewport sizes.

file_operations.description: In the NavBar component's mobile hamburger menu dropdown implementation, ensure the dropdown panel has a solid white background (#FFFFFF or bg-white) that does not change with scroll state. Locate the mobile menu container element (likely the div that appears when the hamburger is clicked) and apply an explicit solid white background class or style. Remove or override any transparent, semi-transparent, or scroll-state-dependent background styling that currently applies to the mobile menu. Ensure the background color remains white even when the underlying page is scrolled while the menu is open. Verify that nav links remain readable against the solid white background.
